Top U.S. voter concern

The Economy

2 of 2 candidates on record

Jobs, prices and the cost of living.

Michael J. LiPetri Jr.
  • ✓Supports letting Americans keep more of what they earn
“Affordability starts with letting Americans keep more of what they earn.”
Source: Mike LiPetri for Congress (campaign site)

What this means for youHe would vote for further federal tax cuts. As one of 435 House members, they would vote and push for this in Congress; it would only become law with majorities in both chambers and the President's signature.

Thomas R. Suozzi
  • ✓Supports trade deals that bring manufacturing jobs back to the U.S.
  • ✕Opposes tariffs he says raise prices on groceries, cars and building materials
“Get rid of irresponsible tariffs that are driving up prices on groceries, cars, building materials, and everyday goods — while fighting for trade deals that bring manufacturing jobs back to America.”
Source: Tom Suozzi's Five-Point American Affordability Plan (campaign site)

What this means for youHe would vote to roll back current tariffs, which could lower prices on imported goods. As one of 435 House members, they would vote and push for this in Congress; it would only become law with majorities in both chambers and the President's signature.

Top U.S. voter concern

Health Care

2 of 2 candidates on record

Health insurance, costs and access to care.

Michael J. LiPetri Jr.
  • ✓Supports restoring the patient-doctor relationship
  • ✕Opposes insurance companies and bureaucrats controlling health care
“We must restore the bond between patients and their doctors, not insurance companies and bureaucrats who wish to control the system.”
Source: Mike LiPetri for Congress (campaign site)

What this means for youExpect support for measures limiting insurer and government control over treatment decisions. The site doesn't name a specific bill.

Thomas R. Suozzi
  • ✓Supports keeping the tax credits that lower health insurance premiums
  • ✓Supports funding prevention and primary care
  • ✓Supports the WISH Act to make long-term care more affordable
“Protect and strengthen the tax credits that lower your health insurance premiums, invest in prevention and primary care, and pass the WISH Act to make long-term care more affordable so seniors can stay in their homes.”
Source: Tom Suozzi's Five-Point American Affordability Plan (campaign site)

What this means for youPeople who buy insurance through the ACA marketplace would be the most affected by the premium tax credits. Seniors and families paying for long-term care would be affected by the WISH Act.

The Situation in Iran

2 of 2 candidates on record

U.S. policy toward the conflict with Iran.

Michael J. LiPetri Jr.
  • ✓Supports a forceful military response to any terrorist acts by Iran and its allied groups
“Hamas, Hezbollah, the Houthis, and the Terror Republic of Iran must know that any acts of terrorism will be responded to with relentless and unmatched force.”
Source: Mike LiPetri for Congress (campaign site)

What this means for youHe would vote for military funding and action against Iran and allied groups. Congress controls war funding, but the President directs military operations.

Thomas R. Suozzi
  • ✕Opposes spending on the war with Iran
“Stop pouring taxpayer money into a reckless war.”
Source: Tom Suozzi's Five-Point American Affordability Plan (campaign site)

What this means for youHe would vote against further funding for the war. Congress controls war funding, but the President directs military operations.

Income and Wealth Gap

2 of 2 candidates on record

How income and wealth are distributed, including taxes and wages.

Michael J. LiPetri Jr.
  • ✓Supports lifting the SALT cap
  • ✓Supports no federal tax on tips, overtime or Social Security
“That means building off the success of the Trump tax cuts - including lifting the SALT tax cap to protect New York families and eliminating taxes on tips, overtime, and Social Security.”
Source: Mike LiPetri for Congress (campaign site)

What this means for youHomeowners in high-tax areas, tipped and hourly workers, and retirees would pay less federal tax. As one of 435 House members, they would vote and push for this in Congress; it would only become law with majorities in both chambers and the President's signature.

Thomas R. Suozzi
  • ✓Supports lower taxes for Long Island families
  • ✓Supports restoring the full SALT deduction
“Tom will Reduce the tax burden on Long Island families and work to restore the full State and Local Tax (SALT) deduction.”
Source: Suozzi for Congress (campaign site)

What this means for youA full SALT deduction would mainly lower federal taxes for homeowners in high-tax areas like Nassau and Queens. As one of 435 House members, they would vote and push for this in Congress; it would only become law with majorities in both chambers and the President's signature.
